nodes.content: Characterize when staggered policy effects remain partially identifiable under network spillovers and bounded unmeasured adoption confounding.
requirements: Establish assumptions yielding bounds narrower than outcome-range bounds, distinguishing direct effects from spillover effects.
Achieve at least 95% confidence-set coverage uniformly over the stated confounding and interference class.

nodes.content: Optimize direct and spillover exposure-map contrasts under Γ≤2 adoption-odds sensitivity and overlap; invert independent-network concentration bounds for uniform 95% coverage.
When do exposure-cell outcomes, overlap, and independent-network sampling yield nontrivial Γ≤2 direct/spillover bounds with uniform 95% coverage?
With [0,1] outcomes, valid exposure mapping, ≥0.15 overlap, and Γ≤2, direct/spillover widths asymptotically fall below 2; inversion covers ≥95% uniformly.
Derive staggered exposure-specific Γ=2 bounds; establish strict direct/spillover width reductions and invert independent-network bands for uniform 95% coverage.
Simulate 10,000 independent-network staggered panels with valid exposure maps, Γ≤2 and ≥0.15 overlap; audit direct/spillover widths and worst-case coverage.
Across 10,000 Γ≤2 panels, direct/spillover widths averaged 0.74/0.91 versus 2; lowest tested-scenario coverage was 95.8%.
Derive worst-case Γ=2 exposure-cell bounds and independent-network simultaneous concentration bands; check strict contrast widths and uniform 95% inversion.
Counterexample: one network contains 90% of units; despite Γ=1 and 0.15 overlap, network-count bands undercover under shared outcome shocks.
If independent-network weights satisfy Σw²→0, Γ≤2 and ≥0.15 overlap yield sub-range direct/spillover bounds and uniformly valid cluster-weighted 95% sets.
Prove strict Γ≤2 direct/spillover width reductions; calibrate uniform 95% bands using Σw² and stress-test dominant-network panels.
Compute Γ=2 direct/spillover sensitivity extrema; prove simultaneous Σw²-weighted concentration bands and check whether both contrast widths stay below 2.
Cellwise overlap ≥0.15 limits population direct/spillover widths to 1.70; Σw²-weighted Hoeffding moment-band inversion covers ≥95% uniformly.
Simulate 10,000 staggered panels with maximum network weights 0.04 versus 0.90; compare Γ≤2 cluster-weighted coverage and contrast widths.
With 0.16 exposure overlap and diffuse networks, Γ=2 adoption odds induced 2.55 neighbor-exposure odds; coverage was 91%.
Retain conditional 1.70-width result, but reject Γ=2 neighbor-exposure sensitivity; propagate adoption-level Γ through exposure mapping before inference.
Propagate Γ≤2 adoption-odds through joint network histories; optimize overlap-restricted direct/spillover bounds and invert diffuse-network bands for uniform 95% coverage.
Which joint-history overlap and network-weight conditions yield sub-range direct/spillover bounds and uniform 95% coverage after propagating Γ≤2 adoption confounding?
If target joint-history cells each have ≥0.15 probability and Σw²→0, propagated-Γ bounds are sub-range with uniform 95% coverage.
Derive joint-history propensity envelopes under Γ≤2, bound direct/spillover contrasts, then invert independent-network simultaneous bands and probe rare-history failures.
Enumerate degree-1–8 staggered Γ≤2 adoption histories with ≥0.15 joint-history overlap; optimize direct/spillover bounds and audit cluster-band coverage.
Across tested degree-1–8 histories, population direct/spillover widths peaked at 1.82/1.91; lowest simulated 95% coverage was 95.3%.
HistoryBounds v0.1 contains Γ≤2 joint-history enumeration, separate direct/spillover bound optimization, cluster-weighted 95% inversion, and degree-1–8 audit tables.
Advance HistoryBounds v0.1 to formal uniform-coverage proof; audited sub-range widths and 95.3% coverage are supportive, not guarantees.
Certify HistoryBounds’ population direct/spillover narrowing under propagated Γ≤2 and joint-history overlap; prove uniform 95% coverage using network-weighted Hoeffding bands.
Can 0.15 joint-history overlap certify sub-2 direct/spillover bounds after Γ≤2 propagation, with Σw²-calibrated bands covering uniformly at 95%?
Prove overlap-based contrast bounds for propagated Γ≤2 joint histories; apply simultaneous network-weighted Hoeffding inversion and audit extreme degrees.
Optimize propagated-Γ joint-history bounds at ≥0.15 overlap; check direct/spillover widths below 2 and derive simultaneous network-weighted Hoeffding radii.
HistoryBounds v0.1 factorizes neighbor adoption: Γ=1 marginals and ≥0.15 conditional target-history overlap allow joint odds 5.67, invalidating coverage.
Enumerate dependent-neighbor Γ≤2 histories with ≥0.15 conditional overlap; recompute HistoryBounds direct/spillover widths and worst-case 95% coverage.

Allowing unrestricted neighbor dependence, corrected direct/spillover widths are ≤1.96/1.98 under conditional joint-history propensity ≥0.15; network-weighted Hoeffding inversion covers ≥95% uniformly.
Replace invalid factorization with dependence-robust joint-history bounds; require ≥0.15 conditional overlap and independent-network Hoeffding bands for uniform 95% coverage.
HistoryBounds v0.2 uses dependence-robust joint histories, conditional overlap ≥0.15, and network-weighted Hoeffding inversion for separate, uniformly 95%-covered direct/spillover contrasts.
Does ≥0.15 conditional history overlap preserve sub-range direct/spillover widths under unrestricted neighbor dependence and Γ≤2 adoption confounding?
With [0,1] outcomes, mapped-history consistency and conditional propensity ≥0.15, dependence-robust direct/spillover widths stay below 2 despite Γ≤2 confounding.
Derive dependence-robust propensity lower bounds, prove separate direct/spillover contrast widths, then invert simultaneous network-level bands at 95%.
Solve joint-history linear programs allowing dependent neighbors and Γ≤2 adoption odds; test whether both contrast widths remain below 2.
With ≥0.15 conditional history propensity, dependence-robust population widths were ≤1.96 direct and ≤1.98 spillover across feasible Γ≤2 histories.
HistoryBounds v0.2 replaces neighbor-factorized propensities with joint-history linear programs and reports separate direct/spillover intervals plus network-weighted 95% sets.
Test HistoryBounds v0.2 across 20,000 dependent-neighbor panels (Γ≤2, conditional overlap ≥0.15, maximum network weight 0.04); audit widths and coverage.
Across 20,000 dependent-neighbor panels, mean population direct/spillover widths were 1.21/1.39; minimum tested-scenario confidence-set coverage was 95.4%.
How should HistoryBounds v0.2 adjust simultaneous 95% bands when event-time exposure histories are selected after observing outcomes?
Predeclare K eligible event-time histories; apply K-adjusted network-weighted Hoeffding bands and test outcome-selected direct/spillover coverage.
Simulate 10,000 independent-network panels; select the largest observed contrast among 12 histories and compare HistoryBounds v0.2’s K-adjusted/unadjusted 95% coverage.
Selecting the largest of 12 contrasts reduced v0.2 unadjusted coverage to 88.7%; K-adjusted bands achieved 95.2%.
Reanalyze n45’s 88.7%-coverage failures using K=12 bands; audit selected-history Γ≤2 population widths and post-selection coverage.
Among n45’s selected histories, Γ≤2 population widths remained ≤1.96 direct and ≤1.98 spillover; K=12 bands achieved 95.2% coverage.
Retain v0.2’s dependence-robust direct/spillover bounds; replace unadjusted post-selection inference with prespecified K-history bands for uniform 95% coverage.
Adopt Γ≤2 dependence-robust joint histories, ≥0.15 conditional overlap, diffuse independent networks, and K-adjustment: sub-range direct/spillover bounds, uniform ≥95% coverage.
